security_audit.summary: No malicious intent, prompt injection, or hidden exfiltration behavior was found. The static findings are documentation examples, placeholder credentials, Markdown backticks, and explicit user-configured evaluation settings. The evaluation harness should still be used with scoped test credentials when connecting to untrusted MCP servers.

remediation.issue: Placeholder credentials in examples can be mistaken for real secret handling.
remediation.suggestion: Keep placeholders clearly fake and add a note that users should never commit real API keys or tokens.

remediation.issue: The evaluation harness can pass user-supplied environment variables to a launched MCP server.
remediation.suggestion: Document that users should pass only scoped test credentials when evaluating local or untrusted servers.

remediation.issue: Reference implementations make outbound API calls by design.
remediation.suggestion: Encourage generated servers to use allowlisted API bases, request timeouts, input validation, and safe error messages.

content.value_statement: MCP integrations need clear tools, safe transports, and reliable evaluations. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through planning, implementation, testing, and evaluation for Python or TypeScript MCP servers.
actual_capabilities: Guides MCP server planning from service research through tool selection.
Explains Python FastMCP and TypeScript SDK implementation patterns.
Provides naming, schema, pagination, error handling, and response design guidance.
Covers stdio and streamable HTTP transport choices for local and remote servers.
Includes evaluation guidance and a Python harness for testing MCP tool quality.
Highlights input validation, authentication handling, and safe error messages.
limitations: It is a guide and does not generate a complete server without user direction.
Examples use placeholder services and must be adapted for real APIs.
Current MCP SDK details should be checked against official documentation.
The evaluation harness requires user-provided credentials and connection settings.

use_cases.title: Plan a New MCP Integration
use_cases.description: Map API endpoints into clear MCP tools with names, schemas, and safe transport choices.

use_cases.title: Improve an Existing MCP Server
use_cases.description: Review tool descriptions, pagination, validation, error handling, and structured responses for better agent performance.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Tool Use Quality
use_cases.description: Create realistic read-only evaluation questions and run them against an MCP server.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Server Shape
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new integration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan an MCP server for this API. Recommend tool groups, transport, naming conventions, and validation requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Design Tool Schemas
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn these API operations into MCP tools. Include tool names, parameter descriptions, response formats, pagination, and annotations.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Implementation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced quality review for existing code.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this MCP server for tool clarity, input validation, error handling, pagination, authentication, and response structure.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Evaluation Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Create read-only evaluation questions for this MCP server. Make answers stable, verifiable, and useful for measuring tool quality.

output_examples.input: Plan an MCP server for a project management API.
output: Recommended transport: stdio for local use or streamable HTTP for shared deployment.
Tool groups: project listing, task search, task updates, user lookup, and reporting.
Validation focus: project IDs, date ranges, pagination limits, and response format selection.

output_examples.input: Review my MCP tool descriptions and schemas.
output: Several tool names need a service prefix for discoverability.
List operations should include limit, offset, total count, and next page metadata.
Mutation tools should include destructive and idempotent annotations.

output_examples.input: Create evaluation questions for a read-only GitHub MCP server.
output: Questions should combine search, filtering, and aggregation across repositories or issues.
Answers should be exact strings, counts, dates, or IDs that can be compared reliably.
Remove tasks that require writing, deleting, or modifying repository state.

best_practices: Start with real user workflows, then map them to focused and composable tools.
Use strict schemas, bounded pagination, timeouts, and actionable error messages.
Evaluate with read-only tasks that have stable and verifiable answers.
anti_patterns: Do not expose every API endpoint without clear names and descriptions.
Do not return unbounded result sets or verbose raw API payloads by default.
Do not rely on annotations alone for security-sensitive client decisions.

faq.question: Does this skill build the MCP server automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance, examples, review criteria, and evaluation workflows.

faq.question: Which languages does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Python with FastMCP and TypeScript with the MCP SDK.

faq.question: Can it help with remote MCP servers?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains streamable HTTP for remote servers and stdio for local integrations.

faq.question: Does it include security guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers authentication handling, input validation, command injection prevention, and safe error messages.

faq.question: How does the evaluation workflow work?
faq.answer: You create stable read-only questions, run them with the harness, and compare actual answers to expected answers.

faq.question: Should I check the official MCP documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill recommends checking current protocol and SDK documentation during planning and implementation.
